title: Device-interface accessibility registry (design draft, unreleased)
description: Draft schema for Roadmap 0.2. Each record describes one version-bound device/interface integration path. A record is a durable, updatable entry, not a frozen metric row: fields are grouped so that a fixed accessibility snapshot, a living maintenance state, an evidence grade, and the claims the record must not be used to support can never be confused with one another.

component_score.description: 0 = property explicitly absent from the reviewed public material. 0.5 = partially represented or only indirectly evidenced. 1 = explicitly and completely evidenced. null = unknown: the reviewed material never addressed this component, so it is excluded from accessibility_score and counted in unknown_components. Unknown must never be silently written as 0.

record_id.description: Stable identifier for the registry record. Immutable once published; corrections change fields, not the ID.

vendor.description: The organization that manufactures or originally publishes the device or control software. Public and factual, never used to derive a cross-vendor ranking.

product.description: The specific product or platform line the interface belongs to.

interface_identity.description: The specific, version-bound interface path being described, for example a named API, driver framework, protocol, or firmware path. A record describes one interface path, not a whole product line.

interface_class.description: The structural kind of integration path, used for grouping and filtering, not for ranking.

maintainer_support_declared.description: Whether a public maintainer or support channel was declared and observable at the time of assessment. This is a fixed accessibility fact about what was publicly stated; it is distinct from maintenance_status, which tracks whether that support is still current.

unknown_components.description: Count of the six accessibility components above that are null (unknown). Must equal the number of null values among documentation, api_protocol, licence_clarity, simulator_isolated_testing, examples_reference_implementation, and maintainer_support_declared.

accessibility_score.description: Mean of the six accessibility components, over known (non-null) components only. Measures public interface accessibility conditions at the time of assessment; it is not a device reliability, quality, or completeness score, and it decays into staleness independently of the score's numeric value, which is why maintenance_status and last_verified exist as separate fields.

maintenance_status.description: Current maintenance fact: whether the interface path (vendor or community) shows ongoing upkeep as of last_verified. This is the field that ages a record even when accessibility_score has not changed, and is why the registry is a living artifact rather than a repost of the fixed b2_integration_access.csv snapshot.

last_activity_observed.description: Coarse, source-bound date or date range of the most recent publicly observed maintenance or usage activity (for example '2025' or '2022-2023'), using the same non-precise convention as the underlying metric file's date-relevance column. null when the reviewed material gives no independent activity signal beyond the assessment itself.

last_verified.description: Date this record's fields were last checked by a maintainer against public sources. Drives staleness review, independent of last_activity_observed.

correction_status.description: Record lifecycle state, using the same vocabulary as schemas/knowledge-index.schema.json so the two registries stay operationally consistent.

evidence_grade.description: 0 unspecified, 1 declared, 2 measured, 3 device-validated, 4 independently reproduced. Same ordinal ladder used elsewhere in this repository (see data/knowledge_index/schema_fields.csv). Reported independently of accessibility_score, because field completeness and evidence depth are distinct.

evidence_confidence.description: Submitter or reviewer confidence in the row as coded, not a statistical uncertainty interval.

evidence_note.description: Short rationale grounding the component scores, evidence_grade, and maintenance_status in what the source material actually said.

evidence_sources.description: Public, stable URLs the record is derived from. Comparable in role to forum_provenance in the knowledge-index schema, generalized to allow more than one source.

known_limitations.description: Explicit bounds on what this specific record does and does not establish, for example partial feature coverage or a single hardware generation.

prohibited_claims.description: Downstream claims this record must not be used to support. Every record must prohibit cross-vendor reliability or market-share ranking; additional prohibitions are record-specific.

record_steward.description: Public role or project accountable for keeping this record current. Distinct from maintainer_support_declared, which describes the device's own support channel, not the registry record's owner.
